# Introduction

Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) from wildfire smoke is an important contributor to air pollution in the United States, particularly in the West, with important implications for public health and air quality management. Human-caused ignitions have extended the U.S. wildfire season beyond the period traditionally associated with lightning-caused fires (Balch et al., 2017)(love the citation method and your background for this project!). As wildfire activity and smoke emissions may change over time, understanding long-term trends in smoke-related PM₂.₅ is important for identifying changes in population exposure and informing air quality management.

Drought is a potential influence on the seasonal patterns of wildfire smoke. By reducing vegetation and fuel moisture, drought can create conditions favorable for wildfire activity and associated smoke emissions. (Wang et al., 2022) found that increasing summer PM₂.₅ concentrations in the northwestern United States were primarily driven by increases in total carbonaceous aerosols, with stronger trends under drought conditions. This suggests that drought may play an important role in shaping long-term changes in smoke-related PM₂.₅. (very insightful project background!)

This study will examine long-term trends in wildfire smoke PM₂.₅ across California during summer and fall, the primary seasons of wildfire activity. Sen's slope and the Mann–Kendall test will be used to characterize spatial trends from 2006 to 2023. Pixel-level Pearson correlation analysis will then examine the associations between drought conditions and smoke-related PM₂.₅, identifying their spatial patterns across California. (I like how you explained what each test does as part of your argument)

# Materials and methods

## Materials

- Daily 10km wildfire smoke PM2.5 data, 2006-2023\
  The wildfire smoke PM2.5 product is produced with a ML method, and the overall R2 is 0.63. Model performance varied spatially, with often very high performance at EPA monitors throughout California, the Pacific Northwest, the upper Midwest, and the Northeast and lower performance at monitors in the Southwest and the South. https://www.stanfordecholab.com/wildfire_smoke.

- Drought data\
  Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) data will be used to measure the drought level. The SPEI data cover the contiguous U.S. from 1979 to the present at the spatial resolution of 4 km and are updated monthly. This drought index considers precipitation and potential evapotranspiration to indicate the spatial and temporal extents of drought conditions. The SPEI data can be access through [x](https://www.drought.gov/data-maps-tools/us-gridded-standardized-precipitation-index-spei-nclimgrid-monthly)

Read daily smoke file and check attributes. The dataset `daily_smoke` covers the entire United States from 2006 to 2023. The column `grid_id_10km` contains a unique identifier for each 10-km grid cell and will be used to join the data with the GeoID shapefile.

```{r}
dailysmoke = readRDS("data/smokePM2pt5_predictions_daily_10km_20060101-20231231.rds")

# Check object class
class(dailysmoke) #  "data.frame"

# Check object structure
str(dailysmoke) # 3 variables,`grid_id_10km`,`date`,`smokePM_pred`
# Number of unique grid IDs
length(unique(dailysmoke$grid_id_10km))
# Check dimensions
dim(dailysmoke)
# Check column names (if it is a data frame)
names(dailysmoke)
# Preview the first few records
print(head(dailysmoke))
sapply(dailysmoke, class)
```

Calculate seasonal mean daily smoke PM2.5, retain only summer and fall observations, and return a dataframe containing the Year, Season, and Grid_ID combinations.

```{r data, echo=F, message=F, warning=F}

grid_ids <- unique(dailysmoke$grid_id_10km)
smoke_season <- dailysmoke |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), Year = year(date), month = month(date)) |>
  filter(month %in% 6:11) |>
  mutate(Season = if_else(month <= 8, "summer", "fall")) |>
  group_by(grid_id_10km, Year, Season) |>
  # Sum recorded predictions; omitted zero-smoke days add nothing to the sum.
  summarise(smokePM_pred = sum(smokePM_pred, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  # Divide by all calendar days: summer = 92, fall = 91.
  mutate(smokePM_pred = smokePM_pred / if_else(Season == "summer", 92, 91)) |>
  # Fill entirely absent grid-year-season combinations with zero.
  complete(grid_id_10km = grid_ids, Year = 2006:2023, Season = c("summer", "fall"), fill = list(smokePM_pred = 0))
print(head(smoke_season,5))
saveRDS(smoke_season, "data/smoke_seasonsummerandfall.rds")
rm(dailysmoke)

```

Load the GeoID shapefile, clip it to California's boundary, and join it with the seasonal mean smoke data to create an sf object named `smokeCA`.

```{r map,echo=F, message=F, warning=F}
library(sf)

# Load the 10 km grid shapefile
grid_10km <- sf::st_read("data/10km_grid_wgs84/10km_grid_wgs84.shp", quiet = TRUE)
dim(grid_10km)
head(grid_10km,5)
#Get the data type of every column
print(sapply(grid_10km, class))
# Load the geoshapefile of California
CA <- sf::st_read("data/tl_2025_us_state/tl_2025_us_state.shp", quiet = TRUE) |> dplyr::filter(STATEFP == "06")
head(CA,5)

# Match the CRS and combine California's polygons into one boundary.
CA_boundary <- st_union(st_transform(CA, st_crs(grid_10km)))

# Clip the joined grid to California, retaining its data columns.
grid_CA <- st_intersection(grid_10km, CA_boundary)
plot(st_geometry(grid_CA))

# Spatially Join the 10km grid shapefile with corresponding PM2.5 data by ID
smokeCA <- left_join(grid_CA,smoke_season,by=c("ID" = "grid_id_10km"))
# sf::st_write(
#   smokeCA,
#   "data/10km_grid_wgs84CA.gpkg",
#   delete_dsn = TRUE)

```

Convert the seasonal mean smoke data into raster format

```{r conv,echo=F, message=F, warning=F}
library(sf)
library(terra)

# Check geometry and CRS
class(smokeCA)
table(st_geometry_type(smokeCA))
st_crs(smokeCA)
st_bbox(smokeCA)

# Check attribute columns
names(smokeCA)

# Transform the 10-km grid to EPSG:5070
smokeCA_proj <- st_transform(smokeCA, 5070)

# Convert sf to SpatVector
smokeCA_vect <- terra::vect(smokeCA_proj)

# Align the extent to a fixed 10-km grid so cells are exactly square.
cell_size <- 10000
grid_extent <- as.vector(terra::ext(smokeCA_vect))
x_min <- floor(grid_extent[1] / cell_size) * cell_size
x_max <- ceiling(grid_extent[2] / cell_size) * cell_size
y_min <- floor(grid_extent[3] / cell_size) * cell_size
y_max <- ceiling(grid_extent[4] / cell_size) * cell_size
r <- terra::rast(
  nrows = as.integer(round((y_max - y_min) / cell_size)),
  ncols = as.integer(round((x_max - x_min) / cell_size)),
  xmin = x_min, xmax = x_max,
  ymin = y_min, ymax = y_max,
  crs = terra::crs(smokeCA_vect))
stopifnot(all(abs(terra::res(r) - cell_size) < 1e-8))
dim(r)

# Get unique seasons and years
# Use consecutive years from the earliest to the latest observed year.
years <- seq.int(min(smokeCA_proj$Year, na.rm = TRUE), max(smokeCA_proj$Year, na.rm = TRUE))
seasons <- sort(unique(na.omit(as.character(smokeCA_proj$Season))))
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)

for (ss in seasons) {
  # Initialize one NA band per year so missing combinations retain their positions.
  pm25_season <- terra::rast(r, nlyrs = length(years), vals = NA_real_)

  for (i in seq_along(years)) {
    sub_grid <- smokeCA_proj |> filter(Year == years[i], Season == ss)
    if (nrow(sub_grid) == 0) next

    # Write the existing seasonal means into the corresponding annual band.
    pm25_season[[i]] <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(sub_grid), r, field = "smokePM_pred")}

  names(pm25_season) <- paste0("smokePM_pred_", years)
  output_file <- file.path(
    "data",
    paste0("PM25_CA_", ss, ".tif")
  )

  # Write raster
  terra::writeRaster(
    pm25_season,
    output_file,
    overwrite = TRUE
  )}

```

# Results

Plot the daily mean smoke PM₂.₅ concentrations for summer and fall.

```{r seao, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, fig.retina=2}
library(terra)
library(tidyterra)
library(ggplot2)

# Read seasonal rasters before using them in the mean maps.
summer <- rast("data/PM25_CA_summer.tif")
fall   <- rast("data/PM25_CA_fall.tif")

# plot the summer and fall mean
# Calculate each pixel's mean across years, retaining zero-smoke years.
summer_mean <- app(summer, fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
fall_mean <- app(fall, fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)

mean_maps <- c(summer_mean, fall_mean)
names(mean_maps) <- c("Summer", "Fall")

# Plot summer and fall side by side with a shared color scale.
p_mean <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = mean_maps) +
  facet_wrap(~lyr, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma",
    name = expression(atop("Mean daily smoke " * plain(PM)[2.5],
                           "(" * mu * "g/" * m^3 * ")")),
    na.value = "transparent") +
  labs(title = expression("Mean Seasonal Smoke " * plain(PM)[2.5])) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.position = "right")

print(p_mean)
# ggsave("data/PM25_CA_mean_summer_fall.png", p_mean, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

```

Calculate pixel-level Sen's slopes and Mann–Kendall (MK) statistics for summer and fall.

```{r seasonal-trends, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(terra)
library(trend)
library(Kendall)

calc_sen <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) < 10) return(NA_real_)
  if (length(unique(x)) == 1) return(0)
  unname(trend::sens.slope(x)$estimates)}

calc_mk <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) < 10) return(NA_real_)
  if (length(unique(x)) == 1) return(NA_real_)
  unname(Kendall::MannKendall(x)$sl)}

# Calculate Sen's slope
summer_sen <- app(summer, fun = calc_sen)
fall_sen   <- app(fall, fun = calc_sen)
# Calculate Mann-Kendall p-values
summer_mk <- app(summer, fun = calc_mk)
fall_mk   <- app(fall, fun = calc_mk)

# Combine slope and p-value into two bands.
summer_result <- c(summer_sen, summer_mk)
fall_result <- c(fall_sen, fall_mk)
names(summer_result) <- c("Sen_slope", "MK_pvalue")
names(fall_result) <- c("Sen_slope", "MK_pvalue")

# Save one two-band GeoTIFF per season.
# writeRaster(summer_result, "data/PM25_CA_summer_trend.tif", overwrite = TRUE)
# writeRaster(fall_result, "data/PM25_CA_fall_trend.tif", overwrite = TRUE)
```

Visualize pixel-level Sen's slopes and Mann–Kendall (MK) statistics.

```{r trend-maps, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=9, fig.retina=2}
# Plot the summer and fall trend
library(terra)
library(tidyterra)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)


# Calculate a shared, symmetric color scale for both trend maps.
slope_range <- terra::global(
  c(summer_result[[1]], fall_result[[1]]),
  "range",
  na.rm = TRUE)

slope_limit <- max(abs(as.matrix(slope_range)), na.rm = TRUE)
if (!is.finite(slope_limit) || slope_limit == 0) slope_limit <- 1

# Common map theme.
map_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(6, 10, 6, 10),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9))

# Plot Sen's slope.
plot_slope <- function(x, title) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data = x) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "#2166AC", mid = "#F7F7F7", high = "#B2182B",
      midpoint = 0,
      limits = c(-slope_limit, slope_limit),
      name = expression(atop("Sen's slope", "(" * mu * "g/" * m^3 * ")/year")),
      na.value = "transparent"
    ) +
    labs(title = title) +
    map_theme}

# Plot Mann-Kendall significance.
plot_significance <- function(x, title) {
  sig <- terra::ifel(x < 0.05, 1, 0)
  sig <- as.factor(sig)
  levels(sig) <- data.frame(
    ID = c(0, 1),
    Significance = c("Not significant", "Significant"))
  ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster(data = sig, show.legend = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Not significant" = "grey80",
        "Significant" = "#D55E00"
      ),
      breaks = c("Not significant", "Significant"),
      drop = FALSE,
      na.translate = FALSE,
      name = "MK significance",
      na.value = "transparent"
    ) +
    labs(title = title) +
    map_theme}

# Arrange the four maps.
plots <- list(
  plot_slope(summer_result[[1]], "Summer trend"),
  plot_significance(summer_result[[2]], "Summer significance"),
  plot_slope(fall_result[[1]], "Fall trend"),
  plot_significance(fall_result[[2]], "Fall significance"))

p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
  plots,
  ncol = 2,
  byrow = TRUE,
  guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
print(p)
# ggsave("data/PM25_CA_trend_2x2.png", p, width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

```
